intro: The vocabulary for today's couples and families, and for bringing up children.
p.la pareja de hecho: the civil partnership, the unmarried couple
b1.texto:
**Couples.** Two people can **casarse**, with **una boda**, or be **pareja de hecho**: they **conviven** without marrying.

Before the wedding there is **una despedida de soltero** (or **de soltera**), and after it **el viaje de novios** or **la luna de miel**.

When it ends: **separarse**, **la separación**, **divorciarse**, **el divorcio**. **Tener una aventura** is to have an affair.

**How long.** **Llevan diez años juntos.** **Llevan dos años viviendo en pareja.**

**Families.** **Una madre soltera**, **un padre soltero**. **Adoptar un niño**; **un hijo adoptado**.

**Bringing up children.** **Educar** a un hijo. Small children go to **la guardería**; in the evening **un canguro** looks after them. In Spain **el canguro** and **la canguro** are the same word.

**Behaviour.** **Portarse bien** or **mal**. **Obedecer** or **desobedecer a** los padres. A child can be **travieso** (naughty, said with affection) or **maleducado** (rude, a real criticism). The opposite is **educado**.

**Careful with educado.** It means polite, not educated. A person with studies is **culto** or **con estudios**.

**Arguing.** **Discutir con** los padres. In Spanish **discutir** usually means to argue, not just to discuss.
b2.f0: At Rosa's house three generations and almost every kind of family get together on Sundays.
b2.f1: She married in her grandmother's garden fifty years ago and never thought of separating.
b2.f2: Her eldest daughter is divorced and is a single mother of a rather naughty boy.
b2.f3: Her son has been living with his boyfriend for twelve years: they are civil partners and have adopted a girl.
b2.f4: The youngest married in a civil ceremony last year and still talks about her honeymoon.
b2.f5: Rosa says the only thing she asks is that the grandchildren behave at the table and that nobody looks at their phone at the table.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, who has adopted a child?
b5.pregunta: Es un chico muy educado means…
b5.o0.refuerzo: Educado here means polite or well mannered, not educated.
b6.pregunta: Complete: I always obey my parents.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Verbs in -ecer take -zc- in the first person.
b7.pregunta: Who looks after the children when the parents go out?
b7.o0.refuerzo: El canguro is the babysitter who looks after children while parents are out.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is a place for small children during the day.
b8.o0: They have been living together for five years.
b8.o0.explicacion: Llevan cinco años viviendo juntos uses llevar for a period still continuing now.
b8.o1: They take five years to live together.
b8.o1.explicacion: Llevar + time + gerund: to have been doing.
b8.o2: They lived together five years ago.
b8.o2.explicacion: The action is still going on.
b9.traduccion: The children behaved very well at the wedding.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about how families have changed in your country in the last fifty years.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud on how children should be brought up: rules, freedom and obedience.
